Calculate the area of the regular pentagon. Answer to 1 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 15 pentagon beneath the area instruction
spec.description: Blue pentagon ABCDE with B uppermost, horizontal AC and ED, and diagonal AD. Every perimeter edge has matching black double ticks. ED is labelled 5 cm below. Vertex labels are black and outside the outline.
spec.mathematics: Regularity explicitly supplied; native equal-side diagram and full triangle-decomposition solution preserved.
spec.editorialReview: The description records source appearance; active values and geometry follow the approved correction log.

answer.short: $$\begin{gathered}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle AED)=\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)=11.89\text{ cm}^2\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ADC)=19.24\text{ cm}^2\\43.0\text{ cm}^2\end{gathered}$$
answer.worked:
Each interior angle is $\frac{180(5-2)}{5}=108°$. Each base angle in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle AED$ is $\frac{180°-108°}{2}=36°$.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)&=\operatorname{Area}(\triangle AED)=\frac12(5)(5)\sin108°\\[8pt]AC^2=AD^2&=5^2+5^2-2(5)(5)\cos108°\\\angle CAD&=108°-36°-36°=36°\\[8pt]\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ADC)&=\frac12(50-50\cos108°)\sin36°\\[8pt]\operatorname{Area}(ABCDE)&=25\sin108°+\frac12(50-50\cos108°)\sin36°\\[8pt]\operatorname{Area}(ABCDE)&\approx43.0\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
